correctness.rationale: The exact weighted half-plane kernel is fixed by a Fourier–Laplace integral and matches the normalization of Deng–Huang–Qian, arXiv:2009.02989. Mixed derivatives obey \(\partial_z^r\partial_{\overline w}^sK/K=(-1)^r(h)_{r+s}t^{r+s}\). Expanding four derivative combinations and dividing by a nowhere-zero factor yields exactly \(Q(t)=1+A[(-1)^dc+\overline c]t^d+(-1)^dB|c|^2t^{2d}\). For \(h=\alpha+2>1\) and \(q>p\), strict gamma log-convexity proves \(B>A^2\), so the quadratic in \(t^d\) has two distinct nonzero roots. Complete angular enumeration gives the claimed \(d\), \(d+1\), and \(d-1\) counts and real-boundary cases; all zeros are simple and accessible as \(t=(z-\overline w)^{-1}\) for suitable interior points. The standalone checker passed four high-precision Fourier-integral normalization tests and 560 root tests; the analytic proof, not finite samples, covers all parameters. Limits: no fixed-point-slice count or more-than-two-jet claim.

value.rationale: The canonical differential-sequence kernel construction (Gehlawat–Jain–Sarkar, arXiv:2608.13193, Theorem 4.11) raises the Lu Qi-Keng zero-set problem. Exact counts of attainable zeros of its first separated two-term derivative mixtures form a natural structural classification: every gap \(d=q-p\ge2\) yields zeros; the exact count depends only on parity and the sign of \(\operatorname{Im}c\); and the law persists through all \(\alpha>-1\) power weights and all starting orders. The phase dependence and weight/order invariance are mathematically useful global features, not a small numerical improvement or arbitrary slice. The unrestricted differential-sequence problem remains outside the result.
